contests.incumbentNote: Paxton did not seek re-election; he is running for U.S. Senate against incumbent John Cornyn in the 2026 Republican primary.
contests.raceRatingSource: Historical partisan lean — Texas has voted Republican in every AG race since 1994; no independent forecaster has rated this competitive at the general election level
contests.primaryNote: A Roy–Middleton runoff on May 26 is widely anticipated. No candidate is polling with majority support needed to avoid a runoff (50%+1 threshold under Texas law). A two-candidate Pulse Decision Science poll (Feb. 2026) showed Roy 40%, Middleton 38%, underscoring the closeness at the top.

candidates.priorOffice: First Assistant Attorney General of Texas (under Greg Abbott, 2010–2014)
candidates.notes: Announced candidacy August 2025. Gave up his congressional seat to run. Former federal prosecutor and First Assistant AG gives him the strongest legal-credential argument. Leading in all polls. Tea Party/Freedom Caucus conservative with extensive legislative voting record in Congress available.

candidates.currentOffice: Texas State Senator, Senate District 11 (2023–present); previously Texas State Representative (2019–2023)
candidates.campaignFinance: Self-funded ~$11–12M (personal loans from oil and gas fortune); $5M+ cash on hand
candidates.notes: Galveston-area oil company president and wealthy self-funder. Runs on conservative/MAGA bona fides rather than legal credentials — critics note he is not a licensed attorney. Poses as the 'true conservative' alternative to Roy. Strong grassroots support in the Republican base.

candidates.priorOffice: Former Harris County prosecutor; former state district judge
candidates.campaignFinance: Trails Roy and Middleton; donors include Ross Perot Jr. and Houston establishment figures
keyEndorsements: Texas Department of Public Safety Officers Association
candidates.notes: Longest-serving candidate; former judge and prosecutor. Campaign emphasizes law-and-order credentials and rule of law. Polling in third at 13%; unlikely to force or win a runoff unless significant undecided voters break her way. Included because she clears the 5%+ polling threshold and has significant institutional backing.

candidates.priorOffice: Deputy Attorney General under Ken Paxton; Assistant Attorney General for Office of Legal Policy under AG Pam Bondi (resigned July 2025 to run)
candidates.campaignFinance: Raised $2.1M+; most cash on hand (through Dec. 31, 2025)
candidates.notes: Marine veteran; only candidate with endorsement from Paxton himself. Campaign slogan-level rhetoric ('destroy the left'). Polling at 6–7% with no path to top two without significant undecided collapse toward him. Included because he clears the 5%+ screening threshold and has Paxton's endorsement — a meaningful signal in this primary electorate. NOTE: Ballotpedia listed campaign website as AaronReitz.com but confirmed URL is reitzfortexas.com.

candidates.currentOffice: Texas State Senator, Senate District 16 — Dallas (2019–present)
candidates.campaignFinance: Raised ~$650K during filing period; $750K cash on hand (through Dec. 31, 2025)
keyEndorsements: Dallas DA John Creuzot (indirect — Creuzot stated respect for Huffman but endorsed Johnson)
candidates.notes: First Democrat to announce; leads Democratic primary. Physics degree from U of Arizona; law degree from UT Austin. Business litigator at Thompson Coburn in Dallas. Announced July 15, 2025. Has state legislative voting record.

candidates.priorOffice: Mayor of Galveston (8 years); 2022 Democratic nominee for Texas AG
candidates.notes: Grandson of Watergate special prosecutor Leon Jaworski. 30+ years practicing law; focus on civil litigation, mediation, and municipal law. Second bid for Texas AG after 2022 Democratic primary. Campaign emphasizes voter registration, affordability, and anti-corruption. Polling within margin of Johnson.

First-time candidate. Army veteran (tank commander and JAG officer in Iraq); former FBI Special Agent; former federal prosecutor in the Eastern District of Missouri. Dallas civil litigator at Gray Reed. Investigated $30B in wartime contracting waste for Congressional Commission. Campaign focuses on restoring integrity to the office. Polling third at 13% — included per user instruction to include top 3 Democratic primary candidates; clears the evidence floor.

republicanRunoff.basis: No candidate is polling at or above 50%. Two-candidate Pulse Decision Science poll (Feb. 2026) showed Roy 40%, Middleton 38%, confirming a near-tie at the top two. Huffman at 13% and Reitz at 6% are unlikely to overtake either leader.

democraticRunoff.basis: Johnson leads at 25%, Jaworski at 22%, Box at 13%; with 40% undecided in some polls, a runoff is plausible if no candidate clears 50%.

crossCheckNotes: Ballotpedia and Wikipedia agree on the full field: 4 Republicans (Roy, Middleton, Huffman, Reitz), 3 Democrats (Johnson, Jaworski, Box).
John Bash (initially a major entrant tied to Elon Musk) dropped out April 30, 2025 — 21 days after announcing — due to a family health scare. Not on final ballot.
Aaron Reitz's campaign website confirmed as reitzfortexas.com (not AaronReitz.com as listed on some sources).
Joe Jaworski's website confirmed as jaworskifortexas.com (note: some sources list JaworskiForTexas.com — same domain, confirmed).
Primary is March 3, 2026; results not yet available as of manifest generation date (2026-02-27). All polling data is pre-primary.
No candidate withdrawals in the 30 days preceding manifest generation.

Texas AG general election not rated by Cook, Sabato, or Inside Elections as competitive — Texas has elected a Republican AG in every cycle since 1994. Race rating assigned as 'Safe Republican' based on structural partisanship.
